items.prompt: Every one that (87. d) forsakes for my name his house, or his brethren, or sisters (52. 3), or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, with a hundredfold (om. it shall) be requited to him (verb last), and he shall have besides eternal life.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Distributive each person with a ðe relative; the long disjunctive object list; requital to the person; final-verb control; a second promise of eternal life.
items.essential_meaning: Preserve every member of the house/kin/land list and distinguish the person requited from the things forsaken. Treat the omitted English it shall as an explicit construction target, not omission of the promise.
items.defensible_alternatives: A valid different ordering is not compliant if it defeats the stated final-verb target. Supported uncontracted or selected contracted forms are legitimate only within their taught frame.
items.likely_errors: Dropping sisters or children; treating for my name as a location; deleting the passive/requital meaning; an unexplained final verb.

items.prompt: He gave (sęllan) to each a penny in return for his day’s work.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: sęllan gives an accusative penny to each dative recipient; wið exchange/payment for a day’s work.
items.essential_meaning: Each is distributive, and the work belongs to the receiver in the intended context.
items.defensible_alternatives: A dative ǣlcum or selected gehwǣm can be valid when the intended individual reference is retained; use the selected sęllan model for the source hint.
items.likely_errors: Using accusative recipient, substituting the sell sense merely from the English shape, or treating the payment as opposition.

items.prompt: He sent them into (on, 172) his vineyard.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Send an accusative group into a vineyard with on plus the stated directional government.
items.essential_meaning: Possessor his belongs to the vineyard; them is the object sent.
items.defensible_alternatives: Ordinary attested constituent orders are allowed; the on target remains.
items.likely_errors: Using static location without accounting for the stated into target.

items.prompt: He saw others in (om. the) public place standing (169) idle.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: See others with the object-infinitive construction referred to by §169; idle sense of īdel; bare public-place noun as Cook requires.
items.essential_meaning: The people are seen standing, and idle describes those people.
items.defensible_alternatives: A participial construction can be grammatical, but the selected §169 target is accusative plus infinitive. Item 28.7 separately requires a present participle explicitly.
items.likely_errors: Treating others as another singular; translating idle as physically empty; adding the article contrary to the prompt; misreading §169 as a participle-only rule.

items.prompt: Then said he, Go ye also into my vineyard, and I will give you what (ðæt) is right.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Then narration, a plural command to enter the vineyard, and promised giving of headless ðæt what is right.
items.essential_meaning: Retain both the plural command and the subsequent first-person giving promise.
items.defensible_alternatives: The prior plain future-referent present may be valid if taught for the selected verb; the ðæt hint remains.
items.likely_errors: Confusing relative ðæt with a content-clause conjunction, or using a singular command.

items.prompt: Once more he went out about (ymbe, 172) the sixth and ninth hour, and did similarly.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Repeated going out; ymbe with a time expression; sixth and ninth hours; did similarly.
items.essential_meaning: Ninth must have its actual taught form or visible support; it does not follow from having learned sixth.
items.defensible_alternatives: Equivalent word order is acceptable; preserve ymbe and the two specified hours.
items.likely_errors: Silently omitting ninth, using a cardinal in place of the ordinal, or changing about into exact at.

items.prompt: Then about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing (pres. part.).
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: About the eleventh hour; finding others with an explicitly required present participle.
items.essential_meaning: Retain the repeated outing, the specified time, and the people’s standing.
items.defensible_alternatives: An infinitive may be valid outside the target but does not satisfy pres. part.
items.likely_errors: Using an untaught ordinal without help or substituting a perception infinitive.

items.prompt: Then said he, Why stand ye here all day idle?
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Direct why question; plural stand; accusative duration all day; idle people.
items.essential_meaning: The plural people stand; all qualifies the duration rather than counting people.
items.defensible_alternatives: Word order may vary within taught question patterns.
items.likely_errors: Agreeing the finite verb with day or translating all day as every separate day.

items.prompt: Then said they, Because no man (om. hath) hired (hȳrian, 118) us.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Causal reply with nān mann and finite ne; hȳrian preterite; omit English hath.
items.essential_meaning: Nobody hired the group; one negative proposition.
items.defensible_alternatives: An appropriate negative-pronominal expression can be valid if the explicit hȳrian/simple-past target remains.
items.likely_errors: Dropping ne by English analogy, treating two negatives as an affirmation, or adding a perfect contrary to om. hath.

items.prompt: Truly, when even was come [when it was evening become], then said the lord (hlāford) of the vineyard to his steward (gerēfa, 53), Call (cleopian) the workmen, and pay them (164. a) their hire (mēd).
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Temporal clause with evening-become construction; vineyard owner and steward; call and pay commands; dative people plus hire.
items.essential_meaning: The supplied bracketed recasting governs the evening phrase. The two commands address the steward.
items.defensible_alternatives: A grammatical alternative evening construction can be explained but the key must identify compliance with the bracketed target.
items.likely_errors: Turning become into passive, making workers command-givers, or failing the recipient/payment relation.

items.prompt: Accordingly, when those came that came about the eleventh hour (verb last), then received they each his penny.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Temporal and embedded relative clauses; required final verb inside the identified relative; distributive each penny.
items.essential_meaning: Separate the people’s coming from their later receiving; each receiver gets his penny.
items.defensible_alternatives: Order variants outside the explicitly governed final-verb clause may be valid.
items.likely_errors: Putting only the main verb last; treating each as a singular subject that cancels plural received.

items.prompt: And those, that there (ðǣr) first came, supposed that they should (sculan) receive more (māre).
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Plural antecedent with ðǣr and first; reported expectation with sculan; onfōn and substantive māre.
items.essential_meaning: They expected more payment; preserve the subordinate expectation and the selected receive government.
items.defensible_alternatives: A contextual indicative/subjunctive alternative needs its reporting interpretation stated; target sculan and māre remain.
items.likely_errors: Replacing māre with prior mā merely because both gloss more, or automatically copying an English future auxiliary.

items.prompt: Thou (om. hast) made (dōn) them equal (gelīc) (om. unto) us, which (87. d) (om. have) borne burdens (51. 5) in this day’s heat.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Simple-past dōn object-predicate making them equal to us; gelīc comparison complement; first-person relative reference; plural burdens.
items.essential_meaning: They are the people made equal, us are the comparison standard and the people who bore burdens; retain this day’s heat.
items.defensible_alternatives: A valid predicate agreement variant must retain the dōn and gelīc controls; no perfect is required.
items.likely_errors: Treating us as direct objects of make, ignoring relative person agreement, or reading the printed51.5 hint as an instruction to write the number five.

items.prompt: Take that is thine, and go (om. thy way); I will give unto this (om. one) just (eall) as much as (om. unto) thee.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Singular take/go commands; predicative possession; eall marking exact equal quantity; two dative giving recipients.
items.essential_meaning: The addressee takes what is his; the speaker chooses equal payment for this other recipient.
items.defensible_alternatives: Prior equivalent headless-relative or possessive predication can be valid within the taught target.
items.likely_errors: Giving eall ordinary noun agreement when it is an intensifier; forgetting the second recipient remains dative despite English omission.

items.prompt: May I not do what (ðæt) I will?
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Negative modal permission question and headless ðæt what I will.
items.essential_meaning: The whole question asks permission; will expresses the speaker’s wish.
items.defensible_alternatives: Uncontracted modal ne is expected; do not invent a new contraction.
items.likely_errors: Treating English may as subjunctive morphology alone or reading will as a guaranteed future.

items.prompt: Camest thou not to me to work (wyrcean, 200) for (wið) one penny?
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Negative question about prior coming; wyrcean inflected infinitive of purpose; wið payment for one penny.
items.essential_meaning: Preserve the source’s purpose and remuneration, with singular addressee.
items.defensible_alternatives: Valid question order may vary; actual targetwyrcean and wið remain.
items.likely_errors: Inserting an English-style dummy do, using a nominative penny, or confusing work for payment with work against a penny.

items.prompt: He was (om. a) man (wer) and prophet, mighty in speech and in deed (weorc) before (beforan, 166) God and all (om. the) people (folc).
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Bare man/prophet predicates; mighty in speech/deed; beforan with its governed God/all-people phrases.
items.essential_meaning: Do not translate an indefinite article that the source marks for omission; mighty is predicated of the man.
items.defensible_alternatives: A documented meaning of the selected adjective or an equivalent taught phrase may be valid.
items.likely_errors: Imposing English noun phrase articles; assigning speech/deed the subject role; expanding all people into an untaught sense.

items.prompt: That is the judgment, that light (om. is) come into (on, 172) (om. the) world, and men loved darkness (plur.) rather (swīðor) than the light, because their deeds (weorc) were evil.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Judgment identified by content; simple arrival of light; love with comparative preference swīðor ðonne; plural darkness; factual cause.
items.essential_meaning: They prefer darkness to light because their deeds are evil.
items.defensible_alternatives: A different constituent order is acceptable; preserve the explicit swīðor and simple-arrival controls.
items.likely_errors: Treating darkness as singular, reading rather than as a replacement action, or adding English is to the arrival.

items.prompt: God sent not his son into (om. the) world that he (om. should) condemn the world, but that the world (om. may) be saved (hǣlan, 113) by (ðurh) him.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Negated sending purpose contrasted with positive saving purpose; hǣlan passive with ðurh intermediary.
items.essential_meaning: The negation rejects the condemning purpose; the positive clause states saving as the intended result/purpose.
items.defensible_alternatives: Contextual subjunctive variants can be accepted when purpose remains explicit; use the stated hǣlan/ðurh targets.
items.likely_errors: Negating both purposes, translating the world as the agent of saving, or adding English should/may as arbitrary modal auxiliaries.

items.prompt: Your reward (om. shall) be great, and ye shall be (om. the) children of the Highest; because he is kind (gōd) unto (ofer, 172) (om. the) unthankful and evil.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Future reward with omitted shall; child relation to nominal Highest; kind gōd with ofer plus unthankful/evil people.
items.essential_meaning: The clause describes kindness toward those people, not authority over them.
items.defensible_alternatives: Ordinary future-state alternatives can be valid but the first clause follows the omission control.
items.likely_errors: Treating Highest as an ordinary uninflected name without the taught nominal analysis, or importing a prior unrelated ofer sense.

items.prompt: Give, and (om. it) shall be given you.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Command followed by a dative-recipient impersonal/agentless giving passive; omit it.
items.essential_meaning: Giving is urged, then giving in return to the addressee is promised.
items.defensible_alternatives: The English does not explicitly fix number; accept a consistently singular or plural address if all corresponding forms and the target are valid.
items.likely_errors: Using a nominative recipient, inserting a substantive dummy it, or rejecting an otherwise consistent number choice without evidence.

items.prompt: The disciple (leornungcniht, 43) is not above (ofer, 172) his master (lārēow).
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Negative copula; leornungcniht and lārēow; ofer expressing superiority/rank.
items.essential_meaning: The comparison concerns disciple and master, retaining the personal possessor.
items.defensible_alternatives: Selected nis or supported ne is can be grammatical within the stated negative-system teaching.
items.likely_errors: Assuming spatial above exhausts the sense or treating the disciple as plural.

items.prompt: Show us thy mercy, and grant us thy salvation.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Singular prayer commands show and grant; first-person plural recipients; thy mercy/salvation.
items.essential_meaning: Exact source is Show us thy mercy, not Show ye. Preserve both petitions and all persons.
items.defensible_alternatives: Supported equivalent imperative/subjunctive granting formulas are valid if their target distinction is explained.
items.likely_errors: A phantom printed number error, missing us, or replacing thy with your plural.

items.prompt: Swear (thou) not by (ðurh) heaven, because it is God’s throne; nor by earth, because it is his footstool (fōtsceamul, 43); nor by Jerusalem (Hierusalem), because it is (om. the) city of (om. the) great (mǣre) king.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Singular negative swearing command and coordinated nor phrases; ðurh oaths; throne/footstool/city predicates.
items.essential_meaning: Retain all three prohibited grounds and all three because explanations, including mǣre king.
items.defensible_alternatives: The latter nor phrases may share a recoverable prohibition; repeated full commands are defensible if target and meaning remain.
items.likely_errors: Losing a negative in coordination, translating for by a mismatched preposition, or treating Jerusalem as a productive ordinary-declension noun without support.

items.prompt: Swear not by thy head, because thou canst not make (wyrcean) one hair (hǣr, 47) white or black.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Negative swearing by the head; negative ability; wyrcean object plus white/black predicates.
items.essential_meaning: The addressee cannot make even one hair white or black; both negations have their own clause.
items.defensible_alternatives: Use selected uncontracted modal negation; valid predicate agreement alternatives need the same object.
items.likely_errors: Forgetting the second negation, using ge- prefix without evidence, or treating the color adjective as the object noun.

items.prompt: Be your (plur.) speech thus, It is, It is not.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Third-person wish about singular speech, with plural possessive; direct statements of is/is not.
items.essential_meaning: Plural your does not make the noun speech or its wish plural.
items.defensible_alternatives: A defined ordinary wish form is allowed; retain the explicit affirmative/negative pair.
items.likely_errors: Using a plural finite solely because the possessors are plural, or weakening the contrast to yes/no without accounting for the wording.

items.prompt: Ye (om. have) heard that (om. it) was said, Eye for (for, 166) eye, and tooth (46) for tooth.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Simple-past hearing plus impersonal reported passive; formula eye for eye/tooth for tooth with for.
items.essential_meaning: Preserve the two reciprocal-equivalence phrases; tooth uses its new root paradigm.
items.defensible_alternatives: The exact formula remains the target; ordinary report order variants are valid.
items.likely_errors: Using a modern perfect contrary to omitted have, inserting a dummy it, or regularizing tōð into a familiar strong noun.

items.prompt: He that breaks (tōweorpan, 104) one of (of, 166) these least commandments (bebod, 47), and teacheth (lǣran) men so (verb last), he (sē) shall be named least in (om. the) kingdom (rīce) of heaven.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Headless personal relative, tōweorpan and teaching; of-selected least commandments; final verb in the named clause; resumed sē; passive naming least.
items.essential_meaning: Distinguish one commandment from the least-person predicate and preserve the resumption.
items.defensible_alternatives: Order elsewhere may vary; a valid relative without the required final verb is a target mismatch.
items.likely_errors: Dropping the teaching action, treating the demonstrative resume as an article with no noun, or confusing comparative and superlative.

items.prompt: He that doeth and teacheth it, he shall be called great (micel).
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Personal relative with two coordinated actions; the person is resumed by he; passive called great with micel.
items.essential_meaning: The doer and teacher are one person, who is called great. The source does not demand an added the same expression.
items.defensible_alternatives: A checked personal or demonstrative resumption may vary while preserving the actor and the explicit micel predicate target.
items.likely_errors: Taking it as two agents, inventing a mandatory the same control, or replacing micel with a new unassigned adjective.

items.prompt: Ye (om. have) heard that (om. it) was said in old times (tīd), Kill (thou) not.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Simple-past hearing and impersonal passive saying in old times; singular negative killing command.
items.essential_meaning: The prohibition is quoted content; its second person is distinct from the plural hearers.
items.defensible_alternatives: An appropriate simple-past reported formula is allowed within the supplied passive frame.
items.likely_errors: Treating quoted thou as plural, omitting negation, or automatically imposing English have.

items.prompt: Is it your (sing.) earth?
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Copular yes/no question; singular possessive agreeing with earth.
items.essential_meaning: Exact source reads earth, not oath.
items.defensible_alternatives: Ordinary question order and the taught earth sense are valid.
items.likely_errors: Introducing an oath noun on an OCR error or treating singular your as dual/plural.

items.prompt: He has from his labor what he can.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Possession from labor; headless what clause with recoverable modal complement.
items.essential_meaning: The amount he obtains depends on what he is able to obtain; keep the source’s economical ellipsis with explicit support if needed.
items.defensible_alternatives: A full expressed predicate can be grammatical if the key separates it from the compact target.
items.likely_errors: Treating can as independently meaning possess without explaining its omitted complement.

items.prompt: The sun parched his field.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Sun as subject, his field as object, a checked transitive parching verb in the past.
items.essential_meaning: Preserve agent, affected field and past action.
items.defensible_alternatives: Accept a documented taught dry/parch/burn equivalent with its proper government; do not require a single English back-translation.
items.likely_errors: Using an intransitive burn form as an unsupported transitive or borrowing an unverified prefixed verb.

items.prompt: The roads (weg) should blossom (blōstmian, 118), the roads should bloom, so fair (fæger) (om. a) bride (brȳd, 51. b) shall leave her home (hām).
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Plural roads with modal blossom/bloom; a singular bride to leave home; degree so fair; exact blōstmian hint.
items.essential_meaning: Preserve both parallel road clauses and the following explanation/occasion; use the prescribed blossom verb.
items.defensible_alternatives: Another evidenced blossom verb can be valid language, but an answer must follow the named blōstmian hint to satisfy this controlled item.
items.likely_errors: Omitting a repeated road clause, losing feminine agreement with brȳd, or turning the expressive should into a universal tense rule.

items.prompt: If they can, let them live without me.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Ability condition with magan; selected lǣt command with accusative people and plain libban; without me.
items.essential_meaning: The condition says if they can. The following permission or exhortation concerns their living; the selected let construction is visibly scaffolded.
items.defensible_alternatives: A valid third-person plural subjunctive exhortation can also convey let them live. Distinguish it from the selected singular lǣt addressed to an implicit hearer; both must retain the third-person people and without me.
items.likely_errors: Substituting willan for can, making the hearer the person who lives, or treating the supplied let construction as unrestricted new production.

items.prompt: He never forsakes those that trust in (on) him (172).
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Never with finite negation; forsaking object is the people characterized by trusting on him.
items.essential_meaning: Trust has its own sense and on government; belief and trust must not be conflated from the same English preposition.
items.defensible_alternatives: An explicitly checked trust verb and its on phrase may be valid; preserve never and the relative reference.
items.likely_errors: Omitting finite ne, teaching a new trust frame from a familiar headword without evidence, or losing the object people.

items.prompt: I know truly that my Redeemer liveth.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Factual knowing content clause; truly; Redeemer lives.
items.essential_meaning: Preserve speaker knowledge and the actual predicate about the Redeemer.
items.defensible_alternatives: Indicative factual content is the default here; contextual report alternatives require a defensible interpretation.
items.likely_errors: Misreading living as a required present participle or substituting a knowing-how verb.

items.prompt: In my flesh I shall see God, I (om. my)self, and not (nā) (om. an)other.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Future-referent seeing; in my flesh; emphatic self and constituent nā other.
items.essential_meaning: The speaker is the seer and another is excluded; the seeing itself is affirmed.
items.defensible_alternatives: Order may vary while contrast and nā target remain.
items.likely_errors: Negating the main verb, using the omitted possessive my before self, or giving another the object role.

items.prompt: He was taught (187) to do God’s will.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Passive teaching plus the selected doing-infinitive complement and God’s will.
items.essential_meaning: The person learned to do the will; do not turn God into the learner.
items.defensible_alternatives: A documented taught/passive construction can be valid with the same person and complement; supplied §187 support remains visible.
items.likely_errors: Assuming any participle of teach licenses any complement or confusing will noun with willan.

items.prompt: Lead (thou) us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Singular negative lead command, contrasted positive deliver command; destination temptation and separation from evil.
items.essential_meaning: Retain us as the affected group and the two different relations.
items.defensible_alternatives: Equivalent checked deliver verbs can be accepted if their required preposition/case is respected.
items.likely_errors: Negating deliver as well as lead or treating evil as a personal agent without context.

items.prompt: Be thy name hallowed.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Passive wish about the addressee’s name; hallow meaning.
items.essential_meaning: The name is what is hallowed; the addressee is its possessor.
items.defensible_alternatives: Wesan/bēon or event-focused passive variants can be defensible if taught and appropriate.
items.likely_errors: Using an unanalysed active command or making the addressee the passive subject.

items.prompt: Thy will befall (geweorðan, verb first) in earth as (swā-swā) in heaven(s).
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Initial geweorðan wish verb; thy will noun; comparative swā-swā connecting earth/heavens.
items.essential_meaning: Preserve verb-first source control and the shared occurrence of the will in both spheres.
items.defensible_alternatives: An otherwise valid order can fail the explicit verb-first target; use a separately taught geweorðan form.
items.likely_errors: Substituting bare weorðan without explaining the lexical target, or interpreting will as volition auxiliary.

items.prompt: No king of the English was so great as Alfred.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Nān king plus negative copula; genitive English group; equal-degree comparison with Alfred.
items.essential_meaning: The negative assertion compares every other eligible king with Alfred; do not turn it into a claim that Alfred was not great.
items.defensible_alternatives: An explicit exclusion of Alfred may be defensible in explanation; preserve the source wording and ordinary comparative meaning.
items.likely_errors: Treating negative concord as a positive statement or using a singular invented English ethnonym.

items.prompt: He fought with the Danes (44. 2); he judged his people; he made translations from Latin; he was poet (lēoðwyrhta).
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Four coordinated past assertions: fight, judge, translate, be poet.
items.essential_meaning: All four belong to Alfred; with Danes is the opposed-party relation intended by the context.
items.defensible_alternatives: A documented combat construction or translation expression may be valid; the lēoðwyrhta hint remains.
items.likely_errors: Using accompaniment when opposition is intended without explaining it, or deleting one of the four assertions.

items.prompt: His mother hight Osburg, and his father Æthelwulf.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Defective/inherited naming hight formula; mother and father with proper names.
items.essential_meaning: Exact father’s name is Æthelwulf; preserve both names and both kinship relations.
items.defensible_alternatives: A separately taught passive naming paraphrase may be valid, but the hight expression should be explained if it is the selected target.
items.likely_errors: Inventing a full passive hātte paradigm from one defective form or regularizing the proper names silently.

items.prompt: He lived fifty-two years.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Past lived plus duration fifty-two years.
items.essential_meaning: The numeral phrase receives exact visible support unless a whole higher-numeral system is expressly assigned.
items.defensible_alternatives: Documented order variants of the supported numeral are defensible; no independent numeral recall is assumed.
items.likely_errors: Mistaking duration for a genitive age predicate, or teaching every higher number from this one phrase.

items.prompt: He learned reading after he was twelve (155) years (154. c) old.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Learned reading after a past age state; twelve and genitive years with old.
items.essential_meaning: Distinguish learning as an event from the earlier state of being twelve.
items.defensible_alternatives: A valid past temporal construction can vary in order if the source’s age and sequence are preserved.
items.likely_errors: Using accusative duration for the specified age frame or treating reading as an unsupported infinitive when the selected noun is taught.

items.prompt: His mother had a book of English poems, which she promised (om. to) whichever of her two sons (om. should) first learn it.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Possession of an English-poems book; promise to whichever of two sons first learns it; free-choice and personal/genitive group case.
items.essential_meaning: The recipient is selected by the learning condition. The two sons are her sons; the book is what is learned.
items.defensible_alternatives: Case accommodation or resumptive constructions require the checked evidence and explicit rule; a grammatical alternative is distinct from the selected target.
items.likely_errors: Blindly forcing the same relative form into both external dative and internal subject roles, omitting two, or adding modern should as a separate modal.

items.prompt: Alfred asked her, Wilt thou in fact give that book to one of us two (uncer), (om. to) him who first understands (ongietan) it?
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Direct question after ask; factual emphasis; give book to one of us two with personal uncer; specified earliest understander.
items.essential_meaning: The group contains speaker and one other; the recipient and book have distinct case functions.
items.defensible_alternatives: Taught question order and relative strategies may vary while uncer and ongietan controls remain.
items.likely_errors: Confusing personal genitive uncer with an agreeing possessive or using plural of-us for the dual.

items.prompt: Asser, Alfred’s bishop, wrote a book of (153) the king’s life.
items.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization
items.target: Named bishop with Alfred as possessor/apposition; wrote book with a dependent genitive about the king’s life.
items.essential_meaning: Cook153 marks the specific genitive book-content relation; preserve writer and subject matter.
